title: Best practices — Spirit of the Law
intro: Spirit of the Law (SOTL) is the AoE2 community's go-to source for data-driven analysis. Below are best-practice principles and civilization takeaways distilled from his recent videos, prioritising the last two years.
metaPrinciples: A strong, general economy bonus is the most reliable foundation — it is flexible, forgives mistakes, and lets you 'get away with' many unit choices. The defining bonus of every recent #1 civ is economic (Romans' +5% gather, Vikings' free Wheelbarrow/Hand Cart, Hindustanis' cheaper villagers).
The recipe for a top civ, in SOTL's words: a good economy bonus + multiple bonuses supporting your opening unit + a variety of strong options to transition into later.
Synergy beats raw stats: a bonus that pushes you toward a unit, combined with other bonuses that scale that unit later, is a strong combination (e.g. Mapuche trash+mounted gold-on-kill).

Free or early technologies are worth more than they look — they save resources AND Town Center time (Vikings' free Wheelbarrow/Hand Cart, Chinese cheaper techs, Turks' free Chemistry enabling fast-Imperial).

1v1 Arabia late game is NOT the same as 4v4 closed maps with trade: civs that dominate 4v4 (Celts, Mongols) can fall off in 1v1 late game because their tech tree becomes expensive and one-dimensional.
Know your civ's polarised matchups: some civs are near-auto-win in some matchups and hard-countered in others (Hindustanis steamroll limited-archer/cavalry civs but lose to aggressive infantry civs).
Always be making villagers — the player who trained more villagers earlier almost always wins the macro war; protect that production above all else.
Counter units beat efficient units: Skirmishers into Archers, Pikemen into Knights, Mangonels into massed Archers. Build the counter to the army you're facing, not a mirror of it.
Bonus-damage classes matter more than raw attack — read what your unit counters (e.g. the anti-cavalry bonus on Pikemen/Halberdiers) and aim it at the right target.
Double-Bit Axe is the best-return Feudal economy upgrade; grab it the instant you click Feudal, and keep lumber and farm upgrades rolling through Castle Age.
Cheap-tech civs (Chinese, Byzantines) compound with game length — every discounted technology is resources freed for another unit or upgrade.
Siege is the late-game answer to massed ranged/infantry: Onagers and Mangonels force fights you would lose in a straight shoot-out.
Fishing ships are villagers that cost wood, not food — on water and hybrid maps a strong navy multiplies your economy and snowballs.

romans.takeaway: +5% faster gather/build/repair and doubled infantry-armor effect make Romans strong at any game length — dominant under 20 minutes — with flexible infantry / crossbow / cavalry / siege follow-up.

vikings.takeaway: Free Wheelbarrow + Hand Cart is a huge farming boost that saves two expensive techs and Town Center time — a multi-villager advantage that lets you flex into infantry, crossbows, or knights.

chinese.takeaway: #1 at the very top Elo. Cheaper techs + extra farm food + fire lancers + Chu Ko Nu shine mid/late, but you start down 200 food and need strong game sense to exploit the cheaper techs.

shu.takeaway: Lumberjacks that also generate food fund an archer + fast-siege + War Chariot castle-age push — overwhelming early-castle pressure, though it falls off late (like Celts).

huns.takeaway: Never being housed + wood savings give flexibility to mix stable and archery units; the Tarkan is a high-armor anti-building secret weapon. Scales better at higher Elo (cavalry-archer micro).

hindustanis.takeaway: #1 in both 2024 and 2025. Cheaper villagers are flexible all game; Ghulam (anti-archer) + faster anti-building camels (anti-cavalry) + +2-range hand cannons cover most comps — but hard-countered by aggressive infantry civs.

khitans.takeaway: Pastures (faster than farms) + doubled melee-attack upgrades + faster scouts → Steppe Lancers, a bleed-damage infantry unique unit, and a discounted early Heavy Cavalry Archer — a textbook eco + synergy + transitions civ.

celts.takeaway: Extra wood + fast infantry + fast-firing siege make men-at-arms openings and castle-age pushes brutal — but the 1v1 late game falls off (expensive, one-dimensional tech tree).

mapuche.takeaway: Settlements act as multi-resource camps (wood savings) and train buffed trash; Bolas Riders and Kona generate gold per kill. A slow start that scales strongly into mid/late game.

franks.takeaway: Multiple scout/knight bonuses + cheaper castles; farm food now arrives instantly on age-up and buffed Throwing Axemen complement cavalry. Still the most beginner-friendly safe pick.

mongols.takeaway: Honourable mention: the best scout opening + Mangudai; even better on maps with extra huntables, but Arabia late-game stats are weak.

italians.takeaway: Honourable mention: long bottom-tier on land, steadily buffed until just missing the top 10.
